verdict: Lend in Bengaluru electronics manufacturing — the data call is OK and the news flow does not lower it; back component and instrument makers with real output, not assemblers whose revenue is memory-price inflation.
title: Bengaluru Electronics Manufacturing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**An electronics manufacturer here buys components, boards and enclosures, runs SMT and assembly lines, and sells finished units or sub-assemblies to an OEM or brand.** Cash comes back only after the customer accepts the lot and pays, so the loan is really financing inventory plus receivables, not the machines. **Value sits in the customer relationship and the test/quality capability, not in the building** — which is why a plant with one dominant buyer is a different credit from one with five.

## Where cash and value sit
**Pricing power is thin and margin is made on bought-out content, so a component price move passes straight through revenue without adding cash.** Dixon's revenue rose 47% to Rs.21,794 crore [7] while volumes were broadly unchanged and memory chip prices lifted selling prices [4], and margins compressed [6]. So when a proposal lands, check whether growth is units or price; if revenue is up but power consumption and headcount are flat, ask for the volume split. **Working capital is the real exposure** — Dixon carried a higher working capital burden [7] — so size the limit to the receivable cycle, not to turnover.

## What has changed now
**The national output signal is strong: IIP NIC 26 output +19.3% YoY and +13.6% Apr-to-date [D].** Karnataka is running ahead of India on GST collections (+11.1% vs +6.1%) and electricity demand (+23.3% vs +9.5%) [D]. Locally, Fluke has started multimeter manufacturing in Bengaluru with Class-I Local Supplier status [3], and Rapidus has opened engineering centres in Bengaluru and Hubli for 2nm design work [1] — design work, not fabrication, so it brings salaries and small capex, not component demand. **Sources say little about Bengaluru's own factory-level output; lean on the state data and the peers.**

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue tier-2 component, instrument and test-equipment makers, and local suppliers to Make-in-India programmes like Fluke's [3]** — they sell to many buyers and hold inventory they can pledge. **Avoid pure assemblers whose order book is one brand and whose revenue jump is memory pricing [4]; their margin is the brand's to take.** A rating report on one electronics player shows operating income rising from 1,804.6 to 2,721.8 with OPBDIT/OI at 15.3% [8] — that is the shape to underwrite, and the report is undated, so treat it as indicative.
**Ask for the customer-wise sales mix and the top-buyer credit period at sanction; if one buyer crosses half of sales, ask for a buyer acknowledgement and cap the limit.**
watch: filing gap over one month or turnover fall >20% -> freeze drawing power and visit the plant
inventory days rise while sales flat -> ask for ageing and slow-moving list
units fall while revenue rises -> confirm price-led growth, cut limit
any invoice past 90 days -> seek buyer confirmation and stop further dispatch funding
sector margin compression continues [6] -> reprice or reduce exposure at renewal
